purpose: Zanubrutinib is used to treat certain types of blood cancers, including mantle cell lymphoma, chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), and Waldenström's macroglobulinemia, among others. It helps slow or stop the growth of cancer cells. Your doctor prescribes it based on your specific type of blood cancer.
how_it_works: Your cancer cells have a protein called BTK (Bruton's tyrosine kinase) that helps them grow and survive. Zanubrutinib blocks this protein, like turning off a switch that the cancer needs to thrive. Without that signal, the cancer cells stop growing and eventually die off.
common_side_effects: Bruising or bleeding more easily than usual, low blood cell counts (which can cause fatigue or increase infection risk), diarrhea, muscle or joint pain, rash, cough, and upper respiratory infections like colds are among the most common side effects.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious bleeding, especially if you take blood thinners — tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual bleeding. It can lower your ability to fight infections, so watch for fever or signs of infection. It may cause heart rhythm problems (atrial fibrillation), so let your doctor know if you feel palpitations or dizziness. Avoid grapefruit and certain other medications that can interact with it. Do not use if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is either 160 mg taken by mouth twice a day, or 320 mg taken once a day, depending on your doctor's recommendation. Take the capsules whole with or without food. Try to take it at the same time(s) each day, and do not open or crush the capsules.
